analysis.title: Space Exploration Technologies Corp. (SPCX): Strong Operating Momentum Across All Segments; SI Compute & Monetization Drive Another Quarter of Upward Estimate Revisions (Q3 Earnings Review)
key_insights: GS reiterates Buy on SpaceX (SPCX) and raises the 12-month price target to $245 from $230, after Q3'26 revenue and GAAP EBIT beat Street estimates.

Q3'26 total revenue was $14,575mm, 14% above consensus of $12,809mm and 4% below GS's $15,190mm. The beat versus the Street came mainly from Super Intelligence (SI) cloud service agreement revenue and Starlink adoption across consumer and enterprise/government.

Q3'26 GAAP EBIT was $2,791mm (19.1% margin), 18% above consensus of $2,356mm and 40% below GS's $4,667mm. SI GAAP EBIT of $431mm missed GS ($2,736mm) and consensus ($777mm), largely due to elevated stock-based compensation tied to the Cursor acquisition.
Connectivity was the profit standout in Q3'26: GAAP EBIT of $2,367mm at a 45.1% margin versus 38.0% consensus (+707bps) and 37.2% GS. Revenue was $5,248mm, 7% above consensus.

Management said new compute generates a payback of under one year, which could fall to about 6 months through lower cost per GW and higher monetization rates. Demand continues to outpace compute supply.

Management referenced a longer-term 50/50 internal versus external compute split, though allocation will likely stay dynamic. Compute constraints sit in infrastructure (power, cooling, electrical) rather than chips. The company is targeting buildout capable of supporting 20GW of incremental capacity during 2027.
Management sees line of sight to 2.5-3GW of nameplate compute by YE26 and a potential incremental 10GW in 2027, with an upside case of more than 20GW by YE27.
Q1'27 revenue guidance of $33-37bn came in well above GS and Street estimates. Management also has a December 2026 ARR target of $100bn.

Q4'26 capex guidance came in above GS and Street estimates because additional compute capacity is expected online (about 2.5-3GW by YE26). Q3'26 free cash flow was -$9,805mm versus GS -$2,929mm and consensus -$11,627mm.

Starship is the core economic enabler. SpaceX targets Flight 15 next month with the goal of capturing both booster and ship, a weekly Starship launch cadence in 1H27, and about 2x weekly by end of 2027 as reusability improves.

Connectivity growth is expected to be supported by V3 satellites (versus V2), Starship mass-to-orbit unlocks, and higher Starship launch cadence over the next 2-3 years. A possible investor teach-in on Starlink Mobile is a catalyst away from earnings. SpaceX also announced an agreement to acquire licenses related to 800 MHz spectrum.
GS cut 2026E GAAP EBIT to $5,406mm from $12,855mm and 4Q26E to $4,709mm from $10,273mm. 2026E FCF goes to -$55,547mm from -$29,475mm, and 4Q26E FCF to -$21,919mm from -$2,731mm.
GS raised 2027E revenue 51% to $192,493mm (from $127,461mm) and 2028E revenue 47% to $303,121mm (from $205,615mm). SI revenue is raised 70% for 2027E to $153,493mm and 66% for 2028E to $244,194mm.
GS raised 2027E GAAP EBIT 49% to $79,159mm and 2028E 41% to $120,723mm. 2027E GAAP EPS goes to $5.52 from $3.96 (+39%), and 2028E to $7.97 from $7.01. 2026E GAAP EPS is cut to $0.50 from $1.30.

The $245 price target is a sum-of-the-parts on 2029 estimates: Space 9.5x EV/Sales (unchanged), Connectivity 20.0x EV/GAAP EBIT (from 24.0x), SI 25.0x EV/GAAP EBIT (from 28.0x). The total is discounted 1.25 years at 12%, with net debt of $93,839mm and 13,250mm diluted shares.
GS's scenario values are $110 downside (-31%), $245 base (+53%) and $330 upside (+107%). Shares are about 25% below the post-IPO peak close, and GS sees a positive risk/reward skew.

Special committees of independent directors at SpaceX and Tesla have formed to discuss a potential business combination. GS offers no view on its likelihood or merits but says future disclosures will likely be important for investors.
GS flags that elevated capital intensity across 2H26 and 2027 means potential future funding needs will likely weigh on the stock until visibility on capital raises improves.

market_movers.rationale: Revenue and GAAP EBIT beat Street in Q3'26, with strong compute scaling and Q1'27 revenue guide of $33-37bn well above estimates. Price target raised to $245 from $230, a base case 53% above the $171.09 close shown in the PT history table (Oct 5 report date).

earnings_insights: SpaceX Q3'26 reported (GAAP): total revenue $14,575mm vs consensus $12,809mm (+14%) and GS estimate $15,190mm (-4%).

Q3'26 reported segment revenue: Space $1,767mm vs consensus $1,458mm (+21%); Connectivity $5,248mm vs consensus $4,917mm (+7%); Super Intelligence $7,560mm vs consensus $6,435mm (+17%) and GS $8,262mm (-8%).
Q3'26 reported GAAP EBIT $2,791mm (19.1% margin) vs consensus $2,356mm (18.4%) and GS $4,667mm (30.7%).
Q3'26 reported segment GAAP EBIT: Space -$7mm (vs consensus -$291mm); Connectivity $2,367mm (45.1% margin vs 38.0% consensus); SI $431mm (5.7% margin vs consensus $777mm, 12.1%).
Q3'26 reported free cash flow was -$9,805mm vs consensus -$11,627mm and GS estimate -$2,929mm.
Company guidance: Q1'27 revenue $33-37bn, well ahead of GS and Street. Management's December 2026 ARR target is $100bn.
GS estimate changes (new vs old): 4Q26E revenue $23,973mm vs $23,925mm; 2026E revenue $51,056mm vs $51,623mm; 2027E $192,493mm vs $127,461mm; 2028E $303,121mm vs $205,615mm.
GS estimate changes: 2026E adjusted EBITDA $24,954mm vs $29,139mm; 2027E $116,680mm vs $83,893mm; 2028E $194,144mm vs $141,162mm.
GS estimate changes: 2027E FCF -$172,008mm vs -$136,134mm; 2028E FCF -$38,366mm vs -$47,179mm.
risk_factors: Governance: majority voting power is concentrated in the founder and CEO, and related-party transactions exist across companies tied to the founder.
High capital intensity and FCF burn will require sizable future fund raises, with potential equity dilution from stock grants, compensation and equity raises.

Space: competition from other launch companies, higher-than-expected internal launch allocation, reliance on government contracts, regulatory approval delays, and lower profitability from fixed-price contracts.

Connectivity: competition from broadband and mobile providers, reliance on Starship (full reusability not yet proven), ability to scale enterprise and government Starlink contracts, reliance on third parties for distribution and spectrum, and licensing delays.

SI: reliance on developing and scaling orbital datacenter compute, competition from other frontier AI models, ability to scale consumer AI revenue, Starship dependence, and supply chain reliance on third parties such as NVDA GPUs.
Power, cooling and electrical infrastructure are bottlenecks for compute buildout.
Broader macroeconomic conditions could adversely affect the business.
vol_and_positioning: Shares are about 25% below the peak closing price after the IPO, which GS cites as supporting a positive risk/reward skew.
Potential future capital raises are flagged as an overhang on the stock until funding visibility improves.
